Synthetic Java interoperability packets for an explicitly unrecorded service date.

These are new regression fixtures, not edits to the frozen shared M0 vectors.
The sender owner generated them through App.deliveryDocument, configured
PDFSigningUtil PAdES and compact ES256 signing, and DeliveryComposer HPKE.
They use the existing shared fixture's public FAKE key derivation and receiver,
not any live native or clinic keys. No PKCS12/keyring is included.

java-unknown-date-canonical-v1.json: embedded PDF service_date is explicit null;
delivery manifest service_date is the required string "".
SHA256 2bc603a3ea3311a14fde89d93b02a4f0632972fa25a1410227199e95eeee37f8

java-unknown-date-legacy-v1.json: embedded PDF and delivery manifest service_date
are both "", preserving compatibility with already signed legacy copies.
SHA256 c1bedde7b8415fda7c886e60697da0460c7490b439624e2a34a6f74a8c117ccb

Routine tests verify HPKE/ES256 and the actual original PDF CMS signature using
the provided ranges and exact embedded manifest, then save/reopen the encrypted
original, custody/history and retained receipt. Explicit ignored tests use the
real confined helper and production receive path for both positive packets and
unknown/known conflicts. They do not establish Windows UI or live portal behavior.
No service date is inferred from the fixture clock, PDF issue time or Date added.
